sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是 Benjamin Poulin，我是 Mark Ronson，欢迎收听《The Reframers》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其周边文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 即使是在我还在夜店里用黑胶唱片打碟的那个年代，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你每天晚上都要带上 300 件最珍贵的宝贝去工作，把 DJ 台变成了一个充满 50 年历史精美文物的流动博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼（Audemars Piguet）出品的《The Reframers》吧。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的 Michael Barbaro。

sentences.en: This is A Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《The Daily》节目。

sentences.en: Today, the story behind the ambitious new global agreement to protect the planet that you probably haven't heard of.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们要讲述一项雄心勃勃的全球新协议背后的故事，你可能还没听说过它。

sentences.en: My colleague, Katrin Einhorn, explains.
sentences.zh: 我的同事 Katrin Einhorn 将为大家解读。

sentences.en: Friday, January 6th.
sentences.zh: 1 月 6 日，星期五。

sentences.en: Katrin, as 2022 came to a close, something really big happened in your corner of the world that I think escaped the attention of the rest of us.
sentences.zh: Katrin，2022 年临近尾声时，在你所关注的领域发生了一件大事，我觉得我们大多数人都没注意到。

sentences.en: Even though it's not really just my corner.
sentences.zh: 虽然这不仅仅是我关注的领域。

sentences.en: It's not your corner of the world.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是你关注的领域。

sentences.en: I mean, if you think it's all, it's nature.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果你考虑到这一切，它是关于自然的。

sentences.en: It's all corners of the world.
sentences.zh: 它是关乎全球每一个角落的。

sentences.en: Something quite historic, actually.
sentences.zh: 事实上，这是一件相当具有历史意义的事情。

sentences.en: So tell us about this thing.
sentences.zh: 那么，给我们讲讲这件事吧。

sentences.en: So listeners are probably familiar with the Paris Agreement, this big global agreement to limit climate change.
sentences.zh: 听众们可能对《巴黎协定》很熟悉，这是一项限制气候变化的重大全球协议。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: The world locking hands, dozens of countries, and saying we are going to do something about carbon emissions.
sentences.zh: 全世界携手合作，几十个国家共同承诺要采取行动减少碳排放。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So similarly, countries of the world came together just now in December in Montreal and said we're going to tackle this big other crisis, biodiversity loss.
sentences.zh: 同样地，各国在去年 12 月齐聚蒙特利尔，表示要共同应对另一场重大危机：生物多样性丧失。

sentences.en: In an agreement of the same scale.
sentences.zh: 这是一项同样规模的协议。

sentences.en: Arguably similar.
sentences.zh: 可以说差不多。

sentences.en: Lots of people there really talked about it as a Paris moment for biodiversity.
sentences.zh: 许多与会者确实将其称为生物多样性领域的“巴黎时刻”。

sentences.en: Biodiversity loss is this crisis that has been really overshadowed by climate change, and people are really trying to wake the world up.
sentences.zh: 生物多样性丧失这场危机一直被气候变化所掩盖，人们正试图唤醒全世界。

sentences.en: So tell us about this biodiversity crisis that merited such a historic global accord.
sentences.zh: 那么，请给我们介绍一下这场值得达成如此具有历史意义的全球协议的生物多样性危机。

sentences.en: And I guess on a more basic level, tell us about the very meaning of biodiversity.
sentences.zh: 我想从最基础的层面问起，请解释一下生物多样性到底是什么意思。

sentences.en: Like what is biodiversity?
sentences.zh: 比如，什么是生物多样性？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And why did the world decide to get together and address it?
sentences.zh: 为什么全世界决定聚在一起解决这个问题？

sentences.en: Well, biodiversity is the variety of life on the planet, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，生物多样性就是地球上生命的丰富程度，对吧？

sentences.en: So that includes species and also ecosysteMs.
sentences.zh: 这包括物种，也包括生态系统。

sentences.en: And the biodiversity loss that's happening right now around the world is unprecedented in human history.
sentences.zh: 目前全球正在发生的生物多样性丧失在人类历史上是前所未有的。

sentences.en: Of course, there have been extinction events in the past that are worse.
sentences.zh: 当然，过去也发生过更严重的物种灭绝事件。

sentences.en: But like, you know, the last one of those was 65 million years ago with the dinosaurs.
sentences.zh: 但你知道，上一次发生那种规模的灭绝还是在 6500 万年前的恐龙时代。

sentences.en: So in terms of how long we've been around on the planet, this is worse than it's ever been.
sentences.zh: 所以，就我们在地球上存在的时间而言，现在的情况比以往任何时候都要糟糕。

sentences.en: The global rate of species extinction is at least tens to hundreds of times higher than the average over the past 10 million years.
sentences.zh: 全球物种灭绝的速度至少是过去 1000 万年平均水平的几十到几百倍。

sentences.en: Say that one more time.
sentences.zh: 请再说一遍。

sentences.en: The global rate of species extinction.
sentences.zh: 全球物种灭绝的速度。

sentences.en: Right now.
sentences.zh: 就在现在。

sentences.en: Is at least tens to hundreds of times higher than it has averaged over the past 10 million years.
sentences.zh: 至少是过去 1000 万年平均水平的几十到几百倍。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: So this is a uniquely bad moment for extinction and biodiversity loss.
sentences.zh: 所以，对于物种灭绝和生物多样性丧失来说，这是一个极其糟糕的时刻。

sentences.en: Since humans have been around.
sentences.zh: 自从人类出现以来。

sentences.en: And, you know, you can think of ecosystems as like a Jenga tower.
sentences.zh: 而且，你可以把生态系统想象成一座积木塔（Jenga）。

sentences.en: And in fact, at the global biodiversity talks in Montreal, there was a sculpture of a Jenga tower.
sentences.zh: 事实上，在蒙特利尔举行的全球生物多样性大会上，就有一个积木塔的雕塑。

sentences.en: To make this point, you can take out pieces and for a while it remains standing.
sentences.zh: 为了说明这一点，你可以抽走积木，塔在一段时间内依然能立住。

sentences.en: But scientists don't really understand which combination of blocks that get removed from that tower are going to totally destabilize it and make it collapse.
sentences.zh: 但科学家们并不真正了解，从塔中抽走哪种组合的积木会导致它彻底失去平衡并坍塌。

sentences.en: What we do know is that the more we remove, the more unstable the tower becomes.
sentences.zh: 我们所知道的是，抽走的积木越多，塔就变得越不稳定。

sentences.en: Give us some real world examples of this to kind of grapple with.
sentences.zh: 给我们举一些现实生活中的例子，让我们能更好地理解这一点。

sentences.en: I think we're all really familiar with endangered animals, right?
sentences.zh: 我想我们对濒危动物都很熟悉，对吧？

sentences.en: So like we grew up learning about tigers and pandas.
sentences.zh: 比如我们从小就了解老虎和大熊猫。

sentences.en: And like, P.S., those species are doing really well.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一下，这些物种现在的状况其实很好。

sentences.en: Tigers and pandas, conservation actually works when you do it and you give it the resources it needs.
sentences.zh: 老虎和大熊猫的例子说明，只要你采取行动并投入所需的资源，保护工作确实有效。

sentences.en: But if you look at biodiversity writ large, species are going in the opposite direction, right?
sentences.zh: 但如果你从更广泛的生物多样性来看，物种正朝着相反的方向发展，对吧？

sentences.en: They're plummeting.
sentences.zh: 它们正在急剧减少。

sentences.en: Insects have been called the little things that run the world, right?
sentences.zh: 昆虫被称为“主宰世界的微小生物”，对吧？

sentences.en: They're at the base of the food chain.
sentences.zh: 它们处于食物链的底层。

sentences.en: They're supporting everything above them.
sentences.zh: 它们支撑着食物链上层的一切。

sentences.en: And insects are in real trouble.
sentences.zh: 而昆虫现在正处于真正的困境中。

sentences.en: Take the American burying beetle, for example.
sentences.zh: 以美洲埋葬虫为例。

sentences.en: Have you heard of it?
sentences.zh: 你听说过它吗？

sentences.en: I have not.
sentences.zh: 我没听说过。

sentences.en: So it's actually kind of a big beetle, as beetles go.
sentences.zh: 在甲虫中，它其实算是一种大型甲虫。

sentences.en: It's black with these red splotches.
sentences.zh: 它是黑色的，带有红色的斑点。

sentences.en: And what these beetles do is they search out dead birds and mammals of a certain size.
sentences.zh: 这些甲虫会寻找特定大小的死鸟和哺乳动物。

sentences.en: Can't be too big, can't be too small.
sentences.zh: 不能太大，也不能太小。

sentences.en: Rodents, squirrels, passenger pigeons when they were around.
sentences.zh: 比如啮齿动物、松鼠，还有曾经存在的旅鸽。

sentences.en: And a male and a female work together to bury this dead animal in the ground.
sentences.zh: 雄性和雌性会合作把这只死去的动物埋进土里。

sentences.en: They then make these secretions.
sentences.zh: 然后它们会分泌一些物质。

sentences.en: They wrap it in all these secretions.
sentences.zh: 它们用这些分泌物把尸体包裹起来。

sentences.en: And then the female lays the eggs on or near the dead animal.
sentences.zh: 接着雌性会在死去的动物身上或附近产卵。

sentences.en: And when the eggs hatch, they feed on the dead animal.
sentences.zh: 当卵孵化后，幼虫就以这只死去的动物为食。

sentences.en: But the important thing that they do for, like, us is that all that dead animal stuff makes the soil really rich, right?
sentences.zh: 但它们对我们来说最重要的一点是，所有这些腐烂的动物残骸会让土壤变得非常肥沃，对吧？

sentences.en: So they're actually improving the soil.
sentences.zh: 所以它们实际上是在改良土壤。

sentences.en: So these beetles aren't just amazing in their secretions and wrappings and earth fertilizing.
sentences.zh: 所以这些甲虫不仅在分泌物、包裹技术和施肥方面令人惊叹，

sentences.en: They're doing something quite important for the soil and therefore for you and I.
sentences.zh: 它们还在为土壤做着非常重要的事情，从而也造福了你和我。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And these beetles used to be widespread across the eastern half of the United States.
sentences.zh: 这些甲虫曾经广泛分布在美国东半部。

sentences.en: And they basically just collapsed throughout the last hundred years or so.
sentences.zh: 但在过去一百年左右的时间里，它们基本上绝迹了。

sentences.en: So what's the next example to think about?
sentences.zh: 那么下一个例子是什么？

sentences.en: The classic example is pollinators.
sentences.zh: 经典的例子是传粉媒介。

sentences.en: By which we mean?
sentences.zh: 指的是什么？

sentences.en: Bees and butterflies and bats.
sentences.zh: 蜜蜂、蝴蝶和蝙蝠。

sentences.en: So 75% of the world's crops benefit from animal pollination.
sentences.zh: 全球 75% 的农作物受益于动物授粉。

sentences.en: I do think it's important to say that, like, a lot of our cereal crops, so, like, wheat and corn and rice, those are wind pollinated.
sentences.zh: 我觉得有必要说明的是，我们很多谷物作物，比如小麦、玉米和大米，是靠风力授粉的。

sentences.en: So it's not like they pollinate everything.
sentences.zh: 所以它们并不是给所有作物授粉。

sentences.en: But, like, they pollinate one out of three bites that every American eats, according to the USDA.
sentences.zh: 但根据美国农业部的数据，它们为美国人每吃的三口食物中的一口提供了授粉。

sentences.en: Fascinating statistic.
sentences.zh: 迷人的统计数据。

sentences.en: And what is happening to our pollinators?
sentences.zh: 那么我们的传粉媒介怎么了？

sentences.en: They're doing really badly.
sentences.zh: 它们的状况非常糟糕。

sentences.en: You know, one study showed that the relative abundance of five bumblebee species has declined by 96%.
sentences.zh: 你知道，一项研究表明，五种大黄蜂的相对丰度下降了 96%。

sentences.en: A huge fall.
sentences.zh: 巨大的跌幅。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And so one thing that farmers have done is they've replaced these wild pollinators, say bumblebees, for example, with domesticated bees, honeybees.
sentences.zh: 所以农民们采取的一种做法是用家养的蜜蜂来替代这些野生传粉媒介，比如大黄蜂。

sentences.en: I don't know if listeners know, but, like, honeybees aren't native to the United States.
sentences.zh: 我不知道听众们知不知道，但蜜蜂并不是美国本土物种。

sentences.en: They're domesticated.
sentences.zh: 它们是家养的。

sentences.en: They're trucked around from crop to crop, right?
sentences.zh: 它们被卡车运来运去，从一个农场到另一个农场，对吧？

sentences.en: And farmers pay for beekeepers to bring these honeybees to pollinate almonds and apples and—
sentences.zh: 农民们付钱给养蜂人，让他们把这些蜜蜂带过来为杏仁、苹果授粉，还有——

sentences.en: Kind of like paid consultants to the crop.
sentences.zh: 就像是农作物的付费顾问。

sentences.en: Not consultants.
sentences.zh: 不是顾问。

sentences.en: They're actually—they're like—
sentences.zh: 它们实际上是——它们就像是——

sentences.en: Like contract workers.
sentences.zh: 就像合同工。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: But even honeybees, these domesticated bees, are collapsing, and beekeepers are reporting really large losses and something that they're really struggling with.
sentences.zh: 但即使是蜜蜂，这些家养的蜜蜂，也在大量死亡，养蜂人报告了非常严重的损失，这让他们非常头疼。

sentences.en: So what exactly is causing all this loss of biodiversity across the world?
sentences.zh: 那么，到底是什么导致了全球范围内生物多样性的丧失？

sentences.en: What is behind all these species being in this one's trouble?
sentences.zh: 是什么导致所有这些物种陷入这种困境？

sentences.en: The big intergovernmental scientific panel on biodiversity loss, sort of the leading global authority, has ranked the causes, the drivers, in order.
sentences.zh: 政府间生物多样性科学小组，也就是全球领先的权威机构，已经按顺序排列了这些原因和驱动因素。

sentences.en: Would you like to guess?
sentences.zh: 你想猜猜看吗？

sentences.en: Would I like to guess?
sentences.zh: 我想猜吗？

sentences.en: I would.
sentences.zh: 我想。

sentences.en: What's the top cause for biodiversity loss, number one in the world?
sentences.zh: 导致生物多样性丧失的首要原因，全球排名第一的是什么？

sentences.en: I mean, just based on my news judgments, I'd have to guess it would be climate change.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，根据我的新闻判断，我得猜是气候变化。

sentences.en: Nope.
sentences.zh: 不对。

sentences.en: No?
sentences.zh: 不是吗？

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Um, human destruction?
sentences.zh: 嗯，人类的破坏？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: You know, consumption?
sentences.zh: 你知道，消费？

sentences.en: Change in land and sea use is the way they put it.
sentences.zh: 他们称之为土地和海洋利用方式的改变。

sentences.en: But yeah, I mean, it's basically humans taking over ecosystems for our own purposes, right?
sentences.zh: 但没错，我的意思是，这基本上就是人类为了自己的目的接管了生态系统，对吧？

sentences.en: Agriculture, towns and communities, mining.
sentences.zh: 农业、城镇和社区、采矿。

sentences.en: We take over land and we take over the sea, right?
sentences.zh: 我们占领了土地，也占领了海洋，对吧？

sentences.en: That's the first cause.
sentences.zh: 这是第一个原因。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Do you want to guess on number two?
sentences.zh: 你想猜猜第二个原因吗？

sentences.en: I don't want to guess anymore, no.
sentences.zh: 我不想再猜了，不。

sentences.en: They call it direct exploitation of organisms, which is like hunting and fishing and us actually killing these animals for our own use, animals and plants, right?
sentences.zh: 他们称之为对生物的直接开发，也就是狩猎和捕捞，是我们为了自己的用途而杀害这些动物，包括动物和植物，对吧？

sentences.en: Number three is climate change.
sentences.zh: 第三个是气候变化。

sentences.en: Interesting.
sentences.zh: 有趣。

sentences.en: And that, in the coming decades, is predicted to be the number one.
sentences.zh: 而且预计在未来几十年里，它将成为第一大原因。

sentences.en: Like, if climate change goes unchecked, it will emerge as the major, major driving factor, right?
sentences.zh: 如果气候变化得不到遏制，它将成为主要的驱动因素，对吧？

sentences.en: It's already a factor and it's only going to get worse.
sentences.zh: 它已经是一个因素了，而且只会变得更糟。

sentences.en: Well, let's focus for a moment on number three, because I think one and two are somewhat intuitive.
sentences.zh: 好吧，让我们先关注一下第三点，因为我觉得第一和第二点比较直观。

sentences.en: Humans either move into a place and make it hard for a species to exist or they hunt it, make it endangered.
sentences.zh: 人类要么搬进一个地方，让物种难以生存，要么就是捕杀它们，使它们濒临灭绝。

sentences.en: When it comes to climate change, how exactly does the relationship work?
sentences.zh: 说到气候变化，这种关系到底是如何运作的？

sentences.en: Is climate change a kind of cause and effect relationship?
sentences.zh: 气候变化是一种因果关系吗？

sentences.en: It can be.
sentences.zh: 可以是。

sentences.en: They're so interlinked.
sentences.zh: 它们是如此紧密相连。

sentences.en: Biodiversity loss and climate change are so interlinked.
sentences.zh: 生物多样性丧失和气候变化是如此紧密相连。

sentences.en: So take coral reefs, for example.
sentences.zh: 以珊瑚礁为例。

sentences.en: When waters become too hot, the corals expel the algae that they need to survive and the corals will bleach and eventually die, right?
sentences.zh: 当海水变得过热时，珊瑚会排出它们生存所需的藻类，珊瑚就会白化并最终死亡，对吧？

sentences.en: So animals and plants have certain temperatures and climactic conditions that they've evolved over tens or hundreds of thousands of millions of years to live in.
sentences.zh: 所以动物和植物都有特定的温度和气候条件，它们在几十万甚至数百万年的进化中适应了这些条件。

sentences.en: And if those change, then we'll see how that goes for them, right?
sentences.zh: 如果这些条件改变了，那么我们就会看到它们会面临什么，对吧？

sentences.en: Scientists are racing to try and understand how this is all going to play out.
sentences.zh: 科学家们正在争分夺秒地试图了解这一切将如何发展。

sentences.en: Of course, all of these things build on each other, unfortunately.
sentences.zh: 当然，不幸的是，所有这些因素都在相互叠加。

sentences.en: So, for example, for animals to adapt to climate change, they need to be able to move to new places,
sentences.zh: 例如，为了适应气候变化，动物需要能够迁移到新的地方，

sentences.en: like move up in altitude or move toward the poles where it's going to be colder, right?
sentences.zh: 比如向高海拔地区移动，或者向更寒冷的极地移动，对吧？

sentences.en: However, because of all that land destruction that we talked about before, like they can't get around.
sentences.zh: 然而，由于我们之前谈到的所有土地破坏，它们根本无法移动。

sentences.en: They're hemmed in and climate change is going to wreak a much worse toll.
sentences.zh: 它们正陷入困境，而气候变化将造成更严重的破坏。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So in terms of these two big crises that we now face, I wonder if there's an easy way to answer this, but which is the bigger, more urgent problem?
sentences.zh: 所以，就我们目前面临的这两大危机而言，我想知道是否有一个简单的答案，但哪一个才是更大、更紧迫的问题呢？

sentences.en: Climate change, which we've come to think of as the greatest challenge of our time, or this loss of biodiversity, which is now getting more attention akin to climate change?
sentences.zh: 是我们一直认为的时代最大挑战——气候变化，还是现在越来越受到关注、与气候变化不相上下的生物多样性丧失？

sentences.en: Some scientists are increasingly arguing that they're sort of comparable existential threats.
sentences.zh: 一些科学家越来越倾向于认为，它们是某种程度上相当的生存威胁。

sentences.en: I put this question to Catherine Hayhoe, who's this prominent climate scientist, and she had a really interesting answer.
sentences.zh: 我向著名的气候科学家凯瑟琳·海霍提出了这个问题，她给出了一个非常有趣的回答。

sentences.en: She said,
sentences.zh: 她说：

sentences.en: Climate change presents a nearer-term threat to the future of human civilization.
sentences.zh: 气候变化对人类文明的未来构成了更近期的威胁。

sentences.en: The biodiversity crisis presents a longer-term threat to the viability of the human species.
sentences.zh: 生物多样性危机对人类物种的生存能力构成了更长期的威胁。

sentences.en: Okay, translate that for us.
sentences.zh: 好的，请为我们解读一下。

sentences.en: Basically, like, in a shorter term, climate change is a huge threat to order in the world,
sentences.zh: 基本上，从短期来看，气候变化对世界秩序构成了巨大威胁，

sentences.en: and governments being able to function with all the chaos that climate change could wreak.
sentences.zh: 也威胁到各国政府在气候变化可能引发的各种混乱中维持运作的能力。

sentences.en: But she's saying that the biodiversity crisis, it's a longer-term thing, but she actually is saying that it presents a greater threat to the viability of the human species,
sentences.zh: 但她说生物多样性危机是一个更长期的议题，不过她实际上认为它对人类物种的生存能力构成了更大的威胁，

sentences.en: in other words, our continued existence.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，就是我们能否持续存在下去。

sentences.en: So one, climate threatens how we organize ourselves.
sentences.zh: 所以，气候变化威胁的是我们组织社会的方式。

sentences.en: The other, biodiversity threatens our very future, our very existence.
sentences.zh: 而生物多样性危机威胁的是我们的未来，我们的生存本身。

sentences.en: Because we can't live without it.
sentences.zh: 因为没有它，我们就无法生存。

sentences.en: We can't live without nature.
sentences.zh: 我们离不开大自然。

sentences.en: And with that framing in mind, it seems like, over time, the loss of biodiversity is potentially a greater threat to us than climate change.
sentences.zh: 考虑到这种框架，随着时间的推移，生物多样性的丧失对我们来说可能比气候变化构成了更大的威胁。

sentences.en: Especially given that we're starting to address climate change, right?
sentences.zh: 尤其是考虑到我们已经开始着手应对气候变化了，对吧？

sentences.en: So, like, the curve that we're on with climate change is improving.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们在气候变化问题上的曲线正在改善。

sentences.en: Biodiversity loss is not being addressed in the same way.
sentences.zh: 而生物多样性丧失问题并没有得到同样的应对。

sentences.en: And that is why, in Montreal last month, all these countries came together, nearly every country in the world, to make this new global agreement.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么上个月在蒙特利尔，所有这些国家，几乎世界上每一个国家，都齐聚一堂，达成了这项新的全球协议。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: 33 presidents.
sentences.zh: 33位总统。

sentences.en: I called the president at 4.30 in the morning, and he answered.
sentences.zh: 我在凌晨4点30分给总统打了电话，他接听了。

sentences.en: Seven decades in space.
sentences.zh: 太空探索七十年。

sentences.en: We want to see what's beyond the next star.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看下一颗恒星之外有什么。

sentences.en: 1,000 consumer product guides.
sentences.zh: 1000份消费品指南。

sentences.en: Today, I am testing seven mattresses.
sentences.zh: 今天，我正在测试七款床垫。

sentences.en: 60 super sundaes.
sentences.zh: 60份超级圣代。

sentences.en: They were probably the best team in the league every single year.
sentences.zh: 他们可能每年都是联盟中最优秀的球队。

sentences.en: 53,500 puzzles.
I use a different starting word every day.
sentences.zh: 我每天都用不同的起始词。

sentences.en: 25,000 recipes.
And I love a one-pan recipe because I don't love washing pans.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢一锅出的食谱，因为我不喜欢洗锅。

sentences.en: The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》。

sentences.en: Celebrating 175 years of helping you understand the world and make the most of each day.
sentences.zh: 庆祝175年来一直致力于帮助您了解世界并充分利用每一天。

sentences.en: Subscribe now for a special offer at nytimes.com slash subscribe.
sentences.zh: 立即订阅，享受 nytimes.com/subscribe 上的特别优惠。

sentences.en: So tell us more about this global biodiversity agreement that was just reached by all these countries and how it is supposed to confront the problem.
sentences.zh: 那么，请多告诉我们一些关于各国刚刚达成的这项全球生物多样性协议的信息，以及它打算如何应对这个问题。

sentences.en: So it's 23 targets.
sentences.zh: 它包含23个目标。

sentences.en: There's a really splashy one, kind of the most well-known one, is called 30 by 30.
sentences.zh: 其中有一个非常引人注目的，也是最广为人知的一个，叫做“30乘30”目标。

sentences.en: And countries basically agreed to protect 30% of land and 30% of oceans by 2030.
sentences.zh: 各国基本上同意在2030年之前保护30%的陆地和30%的海洋。

sentences.en: That is a sexy number.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很吸引人的数字。

sentences.en: That's really historic.
sentences.zh: 这确实具有历史意义。

sentences.en: It's conservation at a scale that has never been attempted before.
sentences.zh: 这是前所未有的保护规模。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So how does that work in practice?
sentences.zh: 那么这在实践中是如何运作的呢？

sentences.en: And what might it look like protecting 30% of the world's land and water?
sentences.zh: 保护世界上30%的土地和水域会是什么样子？

sentences.en: So country by country, countries will identify places that they want to protect.
sentences.zh: 各国将各自确定他们想要保护的地方。

sentences.en: And that can mean a variety of things, right?
sentences.zh: 这可能意味着各种各样的事情，对吧？

sentences.en: But what it basically is going to mean is they're going to restrict certain activities that are going to damage biodiversity.
sentences.zh: 但它基本上意味着他们将限制某些会破坏生物多样性的活动。

sentences.en: So they could restrict, say, logging.
sentences.zh: 比如，他们可以限制伐木。

sentences.en: They could restrict fishing.
sentences.zh: 他们可以限制捕鱼。

sentences.en: They could restrict agriculture.
sentences.zh: 他们可以限制农业活动。

sentences.en: And that doesn't mean that people can't do anything on those lands.
sentences.zh: 这并不意味着人们在这些土地上什么都不能做。

sentences.en: But they should be used in a very sustainable way.
sentences.zh: 但这些土地的使用方式必须非常可持续。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Let's get a little specific.
sentences.zh: 让我们具体一点。

sentences.en: What does this agreement imagine would be an example of a piece of land or a portion of the sea that would become protected?
sentences.zh: 这项协议设想的受保护土地或海域的例子是什么？

sentences.en: A national park is like the obvious example, right?
sentences.zh: 国家公园就是一个显而易见的例子，对吧？

sentences.en: So a national park can count.
sentences.zh: 所以国家公园可以算在内。

sentences.en: And already there's 17% of the land already is across the planet is considered to be protected.
sentences.zh: 目前全球已经有17%的土地被认为是受保护的。

sentences.en: That's interesting.
sentences.zh: 这很有趣。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So a national park is an example.
sentences.zh: 所以国家公园是一个例子。

sentences.en: However, there's other examples like the Mayan Biosphere Reserve, right, which is a territory of 2 million hectares in Guatemala.
sentences.zh: 然而，还有其他例子，比如玛雅生物圈保护区，那是危地马拉境内200万公顷的领土。

sentences.en: And local communities have managed that area for like 30 years.
sentences.zh: 当地社区已经管理该地区大约30年了。

sentences.en: So there's sustainable logging, other sustainable use.
sentences.zh: 那里有可持续的伐木和其他可持续利用方式。

sentences.en: It's not like a park where people get kicked out and they can't live there.
sentences.zh: 它不像那种把人赶走、不让人居住的公园。

sentences.en: That is not the idea of 30 by 30 specifically.
sentences.zh: 那并不是“30乘30”的具体理念。

sentences.en: Rather, it's about protecting land in ways that people can use it sustainably.
sentences.zh: 相反，它是关于以人们可以可持续利用的方式来保护土地。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So there's a practicality to this, which is like it's not like 30% of the world will suddenly be rid of humans and industry,
sentences.zh: 所以这具有实用性，并不是说世界上30%的地区会突然不再有人类和工业活动，

sentences.en: but instead will be managed in a more biodiversity-friendly way.
sentences.zh: 而是会以一种更利于生物多样性的方式进行管理。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So there would be restrictions on logging, restrictions on agriculture, restrictions on sort of the most damaging activities, fishing, right,
sentences.zh: 所以会对伐木、农业和一些最具破坏性的活动（如捕鱼）进行限制，对吧，

sentences.en: so that it could be used in a more sustainable way exactly.
sentences.zh: 这样它就能以更可持续的方式被利用，正是如此。

sentences.en: What is the role of the United States in this agreement?
sentences.zh: 美国在这项协议中扮演什么角色？

sentences.en: We're not in it.
sentences.zh: 我们没有参与。

sentences.en: We're not in it.
sentences.zh: 我们没有参与。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: Why not?
sentences.zh: 为什么不呢？

sentences.en: We're one of two like UN countries that aren't in it.
sentences.zh: 我们是联合国中仅有的两个没有参与的国家之一。

sentences.en: The other one is the Vatican.
sentences.zh: 另一个是梵蒂冈。

sentences.en: Like the Holy See.
sentences.zh: 也就是圣座。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Why isn't the United States in it?
sentences.zh: 为什么美国不参与其中？

sentences.en: There's just not the support among Republicans in the Senate is the short answer.
sentences.zh: 简短的回答是，参议院的共和党人不支持。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: But the U.S.
sentences.zh: 但是美国

sentences.en: did send its biodiversity envoy to Montreal.
sentences.zh: 确实派出了生物多样性特使前往蒙特利尔。

sentences.en: She was there negotiating.
sentences.zh: 她在那里参与了谈判。

sentences.en: And the Biden administration has, you know, when he first took office, he did an executive order, which is called America the Beautiful, which is essentially an American 30 by 30.
sentences.zh: 拜登政府在刚上任时签署了一项行政命令，名为“美丽美国”，这本质上就是美国的“30乘30”计划。

sentences.en: So certainly if the U.S.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果美国

sentences.en: was a full member, was a member of this treaty, it would be able to play a much more influential role in places like Montreal when the stuff is being negotiated.
sentences.zh: 是该条约的正式成员，它在蒙特利尔等地进行相关谈判时，就能发挥更大的影响力。

sentences.en: But they sort of did the best they could.
sentences.zh: 但他们算是尽力而为了。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So the U.S.
sentences.zh: 所以美国

sentences.en: is saying that we're with you even if we're not signatories of this.
sentences.zh: 是在说，即使我们不是签署国，我们也与你们站在一起。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And they're, you know, they're kicking in money.
sentences.zh: 而且他们也在出资。

sentences.en: And so they definitely are players in this.
sentences.zh: 所以他们绝对是其中的参与者。

sentences.en: And money is the issue.
sentences.zh: 而资金才是问题所在。

sentences.en: It was the most divisive issue in Montreal.
sentences.zh: 这是蒙特利尔会议上最具分歧的问题。

sentences.en: I mean, for a minute there, it looked like it might derail everything.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，有一会儿看起来它可能会破坏一切。

sentences.en: And why is money so important?
sentences.zh: 为什么资金如此重要？

sentences.en: Well, this stuff costs a lot, first of all.
sentences.zh: 首先，这些事情花费巨大。

sentences.en: Some estimates are like $700 billion a year to do all these things that have to be done, you know, reforming these industries.
sentences.zh: 据估计，每年需要7000亿美元来完成所有这些必须要做的事情，比如改革这些行业。

sentences.en: Like, it's a lot.
sentences.zh: 这可是一大笔钱。

sentences.en: And then on top of that, there's this dynamic which is like, you see the same thing with climate change.
sentences.zh: 而且除此之外，还有一种动态，你在气候变化问题上也看到了同样的情况。

sentences.en: And it's this idea that sort of wealthier countries were able to use their natural resources in order to get where they are today.
sentences.zh: 这种观点认为，较富裕的国家能够利用它们的自然资源才达到了今天的地位。

sentences.en: But now that countries in the global south want to do the same thing, wealthy countries are saying, oh, no, no, you can't.
sentences.zh: 但现在全球南方的国家也想这样做时，富裕国家却说，哦，不，不，你们不能这样做。

sentences.en: For the good of us all, we have to leave the fossil fuels in the ground and we have to leave our biodiversity intact.
sentences.zh: 为了我们所有人的利益，我们必须把化石燃料留在地下，我们必须保持生物多样性的完整。

sentences.en: And when you add colonialism on top of that, right, like these countries literally in some cases exploited the resources of other countries.
sentences.zh: 当你再加上殖民主义的因素时，对吧，在某些情况下，这些国家确实掠夺了其他国家的资源。

sentences.en: And now they're saying you can't exploit your own resources.
sentences.zh: 而现在他们却说你们不能开发自己的资源。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You have to preserve them.
sentences.zh: 你们必须保护它们。

sentences.en: You have to preserve them for all of us.
sentences.zh: 你们必须为了我们所有人保护它们。

sentences.en: Countries are like, OK, then pay us.
sentences.zh: 各国就会说，好吧，那就付钱给我们。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: So an element of this agreement is that countries that are less industrialized are looking to more industrialized countries like the U.S.
sentences.zh: 所以这项协议的一个要素是，工业化程度较低的国家正在寻求像美国这样更工业化的国家，

sentences.en: and saying we need you to subsidize us not using our natural resources in a way that might preserve biodiversity.
sentences.zh: 并表示我们需要你们补贴我们，让我们不要以可能破坏生物多样性的方式使用自然资源。

sentences.en: I mean, that's like underlying it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这就是潜在的含义。

sentences.en: I don't think it's really spoken about more like we need help to do these things.
sentences.zh: 我不认为它被明确说出来，更多是说我们需要帮助来做这些事情。

sentences.en: But the undercurrent is like that.
sentences.zh: 但潜台词就是那样。

sentences.en: So like this Nigerian biologist that I met there named Joseph Monoja, he said they came around and plundered our resources to develop themselves.
sentences.zh: 就像我在那里遇到的一位名叫约瑟夫·莫诺贾的尼日利亚生物学家所说，他们过来掠夺我们的资源来发展他们自己。

sentences.en: And he's like, I'm a conservation biologiSt.
sentences.zh: 他说，我是一名保护生物学家。

sentences.en: I want us to preserve nature.
sentences.zh: 我希望我们能保护大自然。

sentences.en: But he's like, you know, it makes us really mad when then we're told that we can't do the very thing that you did to our country.
sentences.zh: 但他说，当我们被告知不能做你们曾经对我们国家做过的事情时，我们真的感到很愤怒。

sentences.en: Mm hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: So as we learned when it came to the global climate accords, countries like to make pledges and then they never deliver.
sentences.zh: 正如我们在全球气候协议中所了解到的那样，各国喜欢做出承诺，然后却从不兑现。

sentences.en: For example, the U.S.
sentences.zh: 例如，美国

sentences.en: somewhat notoriously has not contributed its part towards the cost of the global climate accord.
sentences.zh: 有些臭名昭著的是，它没有为全球气候协议的成本贡献其应有的份额。

sentences.en: So is there any reason to think that we are going to be contributing a lot of money towards this global biodiversity accord?
sentences.zh: 那么，有什么理由认为我们将为这项全球生物多样性协议投入大量资金呢？

sentences.en: Some of the money is already it's like tied up in U.S.
sentences.zh: 部分资金已经与美国的

sentences.en: aid and things.
sentences.zh: 援助项目等挂钩了。

sentences.en: And that is there.
sentences.zh: 这部分是有的。

sentences.en: I mean, the bigger question is, is this agreement going to work at all?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，更大的问题是，这项协议到底会不会奏效？

sentences.en: Are these targets going to be met at all?
sentences.zh: 这些目标到底能不能实现？

sentences.en: I mean, that was my next question.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那是我下一个要问的问题。

sentences.en: Sorry, sorry.
sentences.zh: 抱歉，抱歉。

sentences.en: No, let's go there.
sentences.zh: 不，我们继续谈这个。

sentences.en: I mean, the inevitable question when we're talking about a follow up to a global climate accord is,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，当我们谈论全球气候协议的后续行动时，不可避免的问题是，

sentences.en: didn't we see that movie already and we realize that we're better at promising things and delivering it the whole world?
sentences.zh: 我们不是已经看过那部电影了吗？我们意识到比起兑现承诺，全世界更擅长许下承诺？

sentences.en: That's really the question.
sentences.zh: 这确实是问题的关键。

sentences.en: Previous attempts at this kind of thing have failed miserably.
sentences.zh: 之前在这方面的尝试都惨败了。

sentences.en: And these targets are super ambitious.
sentences.zh: 而且这些目标雄心勃勃。

sentences.en: I mean, it would require like reforming agriculture and forestry and fishing in major ways.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这将需要以重大方式改革农业、林业和渔业。

sentences.en: Because they really do tackle these causes of biodiversity loss.
sentences.zh: 因为它们确实在着手解决这些导致生物多样性丧失的根源。

sentences.en: But to change that is like transformational change.
sentences.zh: 但要改变这一点，就像是一场变革性的转变。

sentences.en: And we're trying to do that in eight years.
sentences.zh: 而我们正试图在八年内做到这一点。

sentences.en: Seven.
sentences.zh: 七年。
现在是2023年。

sentences.en: And, you know, really, it's not legally binding.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，说实话，这并没有法律约束力。

sentences.en: So really what's in it for countries is that they're just going to be sort of named and shamed if they're not keeping to their targets.
sentences.zh: 所以对各国来说，真正的利害关系在于，如果他们不遵守目标，就会受到某种程度的指责和羞辱。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: So let's talk about what happens if these lofty goals don't get met.
sentences.zh: 那么我们来谈谈如果这些崇高的目标没有实现会发生什么。

sentences.en: What does it look like?
sentences.zh: 那会是什么样子？

sentences.en: These goals are so lofty.
sentences.zh: 这些目标太崇高了。

sentences.en: They're actually like setting out to halt and reverse biodiversity loss by 2030, right?
sentences.zh: 它们实际上是设定在2030年前阻止并扭转生物多样性的丧失，对吧？

sentences.en: That seems impossible, just given reality.
sentences.zh: 考虑到现实情况，这似乎是不可能的。

sentences.en: But the goals are set high like that because, you know, the idea is to get countries as close as they can, right?
sentences.zh: 但目标设定得这么高，是因为，你知道，其理念是让各国尽可能地接近目标，对吧？

sentences.en: And so there's obviously many different ways that it turns out.
sentences.zh: 显然，最终结果会有很多种不同的可能。

sentences.en: And how people are sort of bending the curve on biodiversity loss is the answer to that question, right?
sentences.zh: 而人们如何扭转生物多样性丧失的趋势，就是那个问题的答案，对吧？

sentences.en: There's not one.
sentences.zh: 没有唯一的答案。

sentences.en: It's not like there's two outcomes, a succeed and a fail.
sentences.zh: 并不是说只有两种结果，成功或失败。

sentences.en: I think it's a potential middle ground.
sentences.zh: 我认为存在一个潜在的中间地带。

sentences.en: All kinds of middle grounds, right?
sentences.zh: 各种各样的中间地带，对吧？

sentences.en: Well, let's talk about what happens if perhaps we don't fail and we don't massively succeed, but we're in this middle ground when it comes to biodiversity.
sentences.zh: 好吧，让我们谈谈如果我们没有失败，也没有取得巨大的成功，而是处于生物多样性的中间地带时会发生什么。

sentences.en: It feels like that then means we have to do something similar to what we do when it comes to climate change.
sentences.zh: 感觉这意味着我们必须采取类似于应对气候变化时所做的事情。

sentences.en: We have to adapt.
sentences.zh: 我们必须适应。

sentences.en: We have to live in a world where both climate change and biodiversity loss are a fact of life.
sentences.zh: 我们必须生活在一个气候变化和生物多样性丧失都已成为既定事实的世界里。

sentences.en: So I want to turn to the question of what adaptation looks like when it comes to biodiversity.
sentences.zh: 所以我想转向关于生物多样性适应是什么样子的问题。

sentences.en: Are there good examples of that happening or potential future examples of that happening?
sentences.zh: 有没有这方面正在发生的好的例子，或者未来可能发生的例子？

sentences.en: Well, we talked about the honeybees earlier, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们之前谈到了蜜蜂，对吧？

sentences.en: The contract honeybee workers, right?
sentences.zh: 那些合同工蜜蜂，对吧？

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And, you know, another thing that we've done just in terms of like how to survive with this growing population that we have is the intensification of agriculture,
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，我们为了在人口不断增长的情况下生存下去所做的另一件事，就是农业集约化，

sentences.en: which is driving biodiversity loss, has also sustained us, right?
sentences.zh: 这在推动生物多样性丧失的同时，也维持了我们的生存，对吧？

sentences.en: So it's this sort of difficult double-edged sword.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一种困难的双刃剑。

sentences.en: We're able to produce more food.
sentences.zh: 我们能够生产更多的粮食。

sentences.en: With less biodiversity.
sentences.zh: 以牺牲生物多样性为代价。

sentences.en: Because we do things like we pull nitrogen from the air with fossil fuels to put it on fields, right?
sentences.zh: 因为我们做了一些事情，比如用化石燃料从空气中提取氮气来施肥，对吧？

sentences.en: And we've done this engineering of seeds and crops to make them have these incredible yields, right?
sentences.zh: 而且我们对种子和作物进行了工程改造，使它们拥有惊人的产量，对吧？

sentences.en: But in doing all that homogenization, it's a huge risk because, God forbid, some disease comes along
sentences.zh: 但在进行所有这些同质化的过程中，存在巨大的风险，因为天哪，如果某种疾病出现，

sentences.en: or there are climatic conditions that change and you need something more drought-resistant.
sentences.zh: 或者气候条件发生了变化，你需要更耐旱的东西。

sentences.en: This invaluable genetic diversity is like our safety net.
sentences.zh: 这种宝贵的遗传多样性就像我们的安全网。

sentences.en: And so even as we intensify things, we're like fraying our safety net that we have, God forbid, something goes wrong.
sentences.zh: 所以即使我们在加强集约化，我们也在磨损我们的安全网，以防万一出了什么差错。

sentences.en: I want to make sure I understand that because it's important and fascinating.
sentences.zh: 我想确保我理解了这一点，因为它很重要且引人入胜。

sentences.en: You're saying in a world where we have a lot of biodiversity, we have a lot of sources of food and therefore a lower risk that any one thing can wipe it all out.
sentences.zh: 你是说在一个拥有丰富生物多样性的世界里，我们有大量的食物来源，因此任何单一事物导致一切毁灭的风险较低。

sentences.en: But in responding to less biodiversity, we have come up with solutions like genetically engineered grain that lots of us rely on that could more easily be wiped out.
sentences.zh: 但在应对生物多样性减少的过程中，我们想出了诸如基因工程谷物之类的解决方案，我们许多人依赖这些谷物，但它们更容易被摧毁。

sentences.en: So in some ways, we're at greater risk in a world with less biodiversity.
sentences.zh: 所以在某些方面，在一个生物多样性较少的世界里，我们面临着更大的风险。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It's the world that we're creating in order to sustain 8 billion people on the planet living with the consumption levels that we live at.
sentences.zh: 这是我们为了维持地球上80亿人口以我们目前的消费水平生活而创造的世界。

sentences.en: But it's a huge risk.
sentences.zh: 但这风险巨大。

sentences.en: We can innovate our way out of all these problems until we can't.
sentences.zh: 我们可以通过创新来解决所有这些问题，直到我们无法做到为止。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And human adaptation, as creative as it may be, you're really saying, is always going to be inadequate.
sentences.zh: 而人类的适应能力，无论多么有创造力，你真正想说的是，总是不足够的。

sentences.en: To some degree.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上。

sentences.en: There's another question here.
sentences.zh: 这里还有另一个问题。

sentences.en: We've spent a lot of this conversation, and in general, when biodiversity loss is discussed.
sentences.zh: 我们花了很多时间进行这次谈话，而且通常在讨论生物多样性丧失时也是如此。

sentences.en: It's about provision of food and water for people and even just the joy that people get out of nature.
sentences.zh: 这关乎为人类提供食物和水，甚至只是人们从自然中获得的快乐。

sentences.en: We make it about us.
sentences.zh: 我们把它变成了关于我们自己的事。

sentences.en: We make it about us.
sentences.zh: 我们把它变成了关于我们自己的事。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: You know, there are millions of species on this planet.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这个星球上有数百万个物种。

sentences.en: And at the core of this, kind of at the heart of this whole debate about biodiversity loss, is how much of the planet are we really entitled to?
sentences.zh: 而这一切的核心，也就是关于生物多样性丧失的整个辩论的核心，是我们真正有权拥有这个星球的多少？

sentences.en: Well, Katrin, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 好的，卡特琳，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: Thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。
